articles.title: Mary Peltola Defeats Incumbent Republican in Alaska Senate Race
articles.summary: Democratic challenger Mary Peltola has defeated incumbent Republican Senator Dan S. Sullivan in Alaska , rounding out one of the tightest and most controversial races of the midterm elections, and marking another notable GOP loss in what is typically a reliably red state. The Associated Press called the race on Tuesday evening, two weeks after Election Day , with Peltola securing 50.1% of the votes against Sullivan’s 45.8%. articles.title: Democrats Now Have the Power to Nullify the Electoral College. Here’s How
articles.summary: After flipping several key state legislatures and gubernatorial seats in this month’s elections , Democrats now have a path to nullify an institution of U.S. elections that has cost the party at least two presidential contests so far this century: the Electoral College. articles.title: The U.S. Has Lost Its Measles-Elimination Status. Here’s What That Means
articles.summary: For more than a quarter of a century, the U.S. has held measles-elimination status, meaning the virus was no longer spreading continuously within the country. Prior to the introduction of the first measles vaccine in 1963, nearly all American children contracted the disease before they were 15, for an annual case count of up to four million, including 400 to 500 deaths and 48,000 hospitalizations. articles.title: What to Know About the Apple Outage
articles.summary: Apple has resolved outages that impacted several of the company's services on Tuesday, including Apple Pay, iCloud, and Apple Support. Thousands of users had reported experiencing issues with multiple Apple platforms beginning Tuesday morning. Apple attributed the problems to an internal update and said that it was in the process of addressing them as of the afternoon.
